# Bounded malformed ADTS inputs

Generated by `tools/codec_benchmark/generate_aac_faults.py` from the first
HE-AACv2 frame in `../aac_sbr_gap/source-hev2-44100-stereo.aac` and its pinned
FAAD FIL trace. The generator verifies both source hashes and element boundaries
before modifying anything. ADTS frame lengths describe the resulting bytes.

| File | Modification |
| --- | --- |
| `header-only.aac` | ADTS header with no raw data block |
| `sbr-truncated.aac` | Keep the core and SBR extension type, truncate the payload |
| `sbr-count-overrun.aac` | Set the SBR FIL count to 269 bytes, exceeding this frame |
| `fill-count-overrun.aac` | Set the following ordinary FIL count to 269 bytes |

These cases must produce no PCM, clear stream metadata, allow complete cleanup,
and allow a fresh decoder to play the complete HE-AACv2 fixture. The simple
decoder API can consume a bad frame and return OK with zero output; a nonzero
public error is not required for safe frame skipping. Late allocation failure
has a separate, stricter test requiring `ESP_AUDIO_ERR_MEM_LACK`.

This is a small regression corpus, not a fuzzer or proof that every input read
stays in bounds. Tests of outer input truncation and recovery on the same decoder
are separate coverage requirements.
